items.contract_clause: "- budget/payment accounting," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1187, under "# 27. Out of scope for this iteration" (:1177) / "Do not add these unless separately requested:" (:1179)
items.implementation: Budget/payment accounting is fully implemented as a first-class feature. State: frontend/core.js:215 `budget:{title:'',year:null,items:[]}` and :216 `spends:[]` in the seed; :296-298 and :325-327 normalize them. Domain logic: frontend/core.js:563-611 `budgetSummary(state)` (총예산/기지출/지출예정/잔액/초과), :613 `spendsOfRecord`, :594-595 `spentRate`/`plannedRate`. Labels: frontend/core.js:179-198 (viewBudget '예산', budgetTotal '총예산', budgetSpent '기지출', budgetPlanned '지출예정', budgetRemain '잔액', budgetOver '초과', editBudget '합본예산서', addSpend, spendModalTitle …). UI: frontend/index.html:53-56 budget section inside the status piece, :96-102 `budgetModal` (합본예산서 editor), :104-113 `spendModal` (지출 등록/삭제); frontend/app.js:367-405 `renderBudget()`, :407-447 budget-item draft editor + `saveBudget`, :449+ `openSpend`, :352-358 `spendSection(rec)` inside the detail surface, :216-226 budget summary face with a spend/plan meter. CSS: frontend/styles.css:491-495 `.bg-bar`. Release notes shipped with the installer also advertise it: .github/workflows/windows-build.yml:226 "예산 - 총예산·기지출·지출예정·잔액".

items.contract_clause: "- project completion percentage," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1188 (§27 out of scope). Reinforced by AGENTS.md:22 "Do not add KPI cards, progress percentages, analytics, charts, status dashboards …" and CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:85-86 "- progress percentages," / "- progress bars," (§2.2 Rejected), :95 "The user specifically objected to these because the system cannot know the true project progress merely from checked steps."
items.implementation: Step-completion percentages and progress bars are computed and rendered in three places. frontend/app.js:209 `const pct=g.stepsTotal?Math.round(g.stepsDone/g.stepsTotal*100):0;` then :212 renders `.st-meter` with `width:${pct}%` and a `stepsDone / stepsTotal` counter; frontend/app.js:244 same `pct` computation, :250 renders ``; frontend/app.js:309 + :315 the same for the group (행사) board. The label itself is a progress label: frontend/core.js:124 `boardProgress:`${S} 진행``. CSS for the bars: frontend/styles.css:280-283 `.st-meter`, :302-303 `.bh-bar`. README.md:23 documents it as a feature: "| 미니 대시보드 · 업체별 | … | 진행률·지연·가장 가까운 일정, 펼치면 업무별 |" and :25 "누르면 참여 업체·진행률·지출로 펼쳐짐".

items.contract_clause: "- analytics dashboards," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1191 (§27); AGENTS.md:22 "… analytics, charts, status dashboards …"; CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:84 "- KPI cards," and :91 "- completion analytics,"
items.implementation: A dedicated aggregate/summary window exists: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:51-69 declares a third window `"label": "status", "title": "현황 (status)"`; frontend/index.html:45-56 `<aside class="piece piece-status" id="pieceStatus">` containing a 행사별 roll-up board (`groupBoard`) and a 예산 roll-up board (`budgetBoard`), each with aggregate counters and meters (frontend/app.js:206-226 `renderStatus()`, :240-256 `renderBoard()` with 진행 중 / 완료 / 지연 counts, :305-320 `renderGroupBoard()`). I am flagging this as probable rather than confirmed because the contract never defines "analytics dashboard" precisely; the counted-aggregate + meter + money roll-up composition is what §2.2/§27 describe, but the mapping is my reading, not a verbatim clause.

items.contract_clause: "## 23.3 Rust/Tauri checks" / "When toolchain exists:" / "- `cargo fmt --check`" / "- `cargo check`" / "- build with current Tauri CLI" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1099-1105. Also §23.4 item 5 "5. run Rust checks," :1115, and AGENTS.md:78 "3. `cargo check` for the Tauri crate when Rust is available."
items.implementation: Neither `cargo fmt --check` nor `cargo check` is run anywhere in the repository. A repo-wide grep for `cargo (fmt|check|clippy)` across *.yml, *.ps1, *.json, *.md, *.mjs returns only the contract's own text (CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1103, :1104, AGENTS.md:78) — zero hits in .github/workflows/windows-build.yml, package.json, build_windows.ps1 or tests/. The only Rust compilation is the implicit one inside `npx tauri build --bundles nsis` (.github/workflows/windows-build.yml:78) and build_windows.ps1:13, which satisfies "build with current Tauri CLI" but not the two named checks. package.json:7-12 defines only `check`, `build:standalone`, `test`, `test:e2e` — no Rust script.

items.contract_clause: "GitHub Actions on `windows-latest` must:" … "4. run JS/browser checks," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1109, :1114
items.implementation: The JS/browser checks are not run on windows-latest. .github/workflows/windows-build.yml:18-20 puts them in a separate `web` job on `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (:20), with the explicit comment at :16-17 that Windows runners are reserved for the native build. The `windows` job (:52-54, `runs-on: windows-latest`) runs npm ci, the NSIS build, a PE-subsystem check, a window-existence check and a screenshot script — but never `npm run check` or `npm test`. Whether the contract's "must" attaches to the runner or merely to the pipeline is not stated, so the severity is a judgement call; the literal clause places item 4 under the windows-latest job.

items.contract_clause: "## 23.1 Browser automated tests" … "Minimum flows:" (CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1068-1085) and §23.4 "8. make build logs easy to inspect." (:1118); AGENTS.md:74 "Run all checks that exist or that you add."
items.implementation: tests/e2e.mjs degrades three failed assertions into non-failing SKIPs, and SKIPs do not affect the exit code. Exact sites: (a) tests/e2e.mjs:222-224 — `const calTop = ps('topmost', ['-Kind','cal']);` then `if (calTop === 'NOWINDOW' || calTop.startsWith('PSERROR')) skip('조각이 TOPMOST 가 아니다', calTop); else check(...)`, so a missing cal window or any PowerShell error turns the always-on-bottom assertion into a SKIP. (b) tests/e2e.mjs:250-252 — `const moved = ps('move', ...); const movedOk = /^\d+,\d+$/.test(moved); if (!movedOk) skip('창 위치 복원', ...)`, and :270 `if (movedOk) { ... }` gates the entire restart position-restore assertion, so a failed window move silently removes the check. (c) tests/e2e.mjs:272-273 — `const rect = ps('rect', ['-Kind','cal']); if (!/^\d+,\d+$/.test(rect)) skip('창 위치 복원', `재기동 후 창을 찾지 못함 (${rect})`)`, so "the window did not come back after restart" is reported as unverified rather than as a failure. The gate: tests/e2e.mjs:53 `const skip = (name, why) => { skips.push(...); console.log(...) }` never touches `exitCode`; tests/e2e.mjs:344-350 sets `exitCode = 1` only `if (failures.length)`, and :349 prints `통과 ... 실패 없음 (확인 못 함 N건)`. So a run in which all three assertions were skipped exits 0 and reads as green. (The skips are at least printed at :343, so they are not wholly silent in the log.)

items.contract_clause: "Do not label a Windows build "verified" until the Windows job is green." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1122; AGENTS.md:83 "Do not claim Windows-native functionality is verified unless the Windows build/job actually ran successfully."
items.implementation: tests/e2e.mjs is NOT run on push or pull_request. .github/workflows/windows-build.yml:299-304 defines job `windows-e2e` with `if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.run_e2e }}` (:302), i.e. it requires a manual dispatch AND the opt-in boolean input `run_e2e` whose `default: false` (:6-9). The workflow comment at :289-298 states the reason (WebView2/DevToolsActivePort on the runner). The push/PR triggers at :10-13 therefore run only the `web` job and the `windows` job. README.md:197 nonetheless states "CI의 `windows-e2e` 잡이 돌립니다." ("CI's windows-e2e job runs it"), which is stale/misleading about what actually runs.

items.contract_clause: "3. automated browser smoke tests," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1257 (§29); AGENTS.md:74 "Run all checks that exist or that you add."
items.implementation: `npm run test:e2e` (package.json:11) is a silent no-op pass on any non-Windows host: tests/e2e.mjs:25-28 `if (process.platform !== 'win32') { console.log('Windows 전용 E2E 입니다. …— 건너뜁니다.'); process.exit(0); }`. So invoking the e2e suite on Linux/macOS returns exit 0 with zero assertions executed. This is documented behaviour (tests/e2e.mjs:16 "Windows 전용. 다른 OS 에서는 아무것도 하지 않고 통과한다."), but it means the command cannot distinguish "passed" from "never ran". By contrast tests/smoke.mjs is a hard gate (tests/smoke.mjs:2060-2063 `process.exit(1)` on any failure, no skip mechanism).

items.contract_clause: "## 23.2 Visual regression screenshots" / "Generate at least:" / "- `1440x900` main dashboard," / "- `1280x720` main dashboard," / "- simulated 125% density check if practical," / "- `330x430` helper," / "- detail modal with full procedure + logs + attachments." / "Inspect screenshots, not only DOM assertions." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1087-1097. Also AGENTS.md:81 "6. Produce/update screenshots at desktop and helper sizes for visual regression."
items.implementation: The browser harness generates no screenshots at all: a grep for `screenshot` in tests/smoke.mjs returns zero hits. tests/smoke.mjs does exercise the named viewports as DOM assertions only (tests/smoke.mjs:61 default `viewport = { width: 1440, height: 900 }`, :491 loops 1920x1080 / 1440x900 / 1280x720, :993 and :1373 loop 1280x720 / 1920x1080, :480 and :855 `setViewportSize({ width: 362, height: 640 })`), which is precisely the "only DOM assertions" the clause says is insufficient. The `330x430` helper size does not appear anywhere. Windows screenshots do exist (tests/screenshot.ps1:209-397 writes proof/*.png, uploaded at .github/workflows/windows-build.yml:157-163) but they are full-desktop/piece crops at runner resolution, not the five artifacts §23.2 enumerates, and they are CI artifacts rather than committed regression baselines.

items.contract_clause: "8. a short `IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` containing:" / "   - what changed," / "   - migration behavior," / "   - tests executed," / "   - Windows build result/link or artifact name," / "   - known limitations." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1262-1267 (§29 "Deliverables expected from Codex", :1251-1253 "A completed implementation should leave the repository with:")
items.implementation: VERIFIED ABSENT. No IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md exists at the repository root (ls of /home/user/WorkDashboard lists AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md, CODEX_START_PROMPT.txt, README.md and no report). A repo-wide grep for the string `IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT` outside .git returns exactly one hit — the contract's own line CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1262. `git log --all --name-only` shows the file has never existed on any branch in this checkout.

items.contract_clause: "7. updated screenshots," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1261 (§29); AGENTS.md:81 "6. Produce/update screenshots at desktop and helper sizes for visual regression."
items.implementation: The three committed screenshots are untouched since the pre-implementation baseline. `git log -1` for each of /home/user/WorkDashboard/preview_main.png, preview_helper.png and preview_v5_detail.png all return the same single commit `01b656d 2026-08-14 baseline: v5 핸드오프 내용물 그대로 반영` — the v5 hand-off commit, dated the same day the contract was frozen. HEAD is `769ac2d 2026-09-04`, with v0.7 UI work in between (`e46db16 2026-09-01 v0.7 (3/3)…`, `5a8f6d0 2026-09-01 v0.7 (2/3)…`). They depict the v5 main-window/helper UI, whereas the shipped UI is the three desktop pieces (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:12-69, frontend/index.html:45). Nothing in the repo references or regenerates them: a grep for `preview_` outside .git returns no hits in any script, workflow, test or doc — they are orphaned files as well as stale ones.

items.contract_clause: "5. NSIS build artifact from a successful Windows run when CI is available," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1259 (§29)
items.implementation: UNKNOWN / not determinable from the working tree. The workflow does produce and upload the artifact (.github/workflows/windows-build.yml:268 `cp src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/*.exe dist-notes/`, :270-275 upload as `work-calendar-helper-windows-x64`), and README.md:176-178 documents it. But whether a Windows run has actually gone green — the thing §23.4:1122 and AGENTS.md:83 forbid claiming without evidence — cannot be established from files on disk, and no run link, run id or artifact name is recorded anywhere in the repo (there is no IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md to record it in; see DISC-SYS-10). Reporting as unresolved rather than asserting either way.

items.contract_clause: "- no arbitrary user-controlled path concatenation," / "- generated IDs for physical storage names," / "- protect against `..`/separator path injection," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1169-1171 (§26)
items.implementation: The WRITE path is compliant: frontend/core.js:344 `SAFE_ID=/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/`, :351-355 `attachPath()` rejects non-matching entityId/attId and clamps the extension, :374 the filename is a generated `uid('att')`, never `file.name`; backups are gated by frontend/core.js:735 `SAFE_BACKUP=/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.zip$/` at :780, :794. The READ/DELETE/REVEAL path, however, trusts `meta.relativePath` straight out of persisted state without re-validating: frontend/core.js:382-383 `fs.exists/readFile(meta.relativePath, {baseDir:appDir()})`, :392 `fsApi().remove(meta.relativePath, …)`, :403 `openerApi().openPath(await pathApi().join(base, meta.relativePath))`. A crafted backup zip can reach this: frontend/core.js:763-775 `restoreBackup` only rewrites an attachment's `relativePath` when a matching payload entry exists (`const data=byId.get(list[i].id); if(!data)continue;` at :769), so a state.json entry carrying a traversal `relativePath` and no matching zip member survives into state. Marked probable, not confirmed: Tauri 2's `fs:allow-appdata-*-recursive` scope (src-tauri/capabilities/main.json:7-9) very likely rejects the resolved out-of-scope path at the Rust layer, and I did not execute this. The rest of §26 is satisfied — see notes.

items.contract_clause: §12 "### Deep-link behavior" / "- clicking a helper card should open/focus main," / "- main should open the corresponding schedule detail automatically." / "Implement with a simple cross-window event/message or shared selection state." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:611-618; §22 H checklist "- [ ] Helper card click opens/focuses main and opens matching detail." :1059; AGENTS.md acceptance flow "- Click helper card -> main window opens focused on the corresponding detail."
items.implementation: `state.pendingSelection` — the shared-selection mechanism — has a consumer but no producer. Every occurrence in shipped code: frontend/core.js:213 seed `pendingSelection:null`, :276-277 v5→v6 migration note + backfill, :317 normalize; frontend/app.js:1056-1058 `consumePendingSelection()` reads it, nulls it and calls `openRecord`, wired at :1183 (`watchState`) and :1184 (startup). Nothing anywhere in frontend/ or src-tauri/ ever assigns a non-null value — grep for `pendingSelection` across frontend/ and src-tauri/ returns only those six lines. The only writers are the test suites: tests/smoke.mjs:381, :1761 and tests/e2e.mjs:240, which inject it by hand. So the field is dead in production and the deep-link is unreachable by any user gesture.

items.contract_clause: "- optional always-on-top," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:603 (§12); §22 H "- [ ] Always-on-top setting works." :1060
items.implementation: `settings.helperAlwaysOnTop` is written into the default state at frontend/core.js:212 `settings:{horizon:'14',customHorizon:45,helperAlwaysOnTop:true,autostart:false}` and is never read anywhere — grep across frontend/ and src-tauri/ for `helperAlwaysOnTop|alwaysOnTop|always_on_top` returns only that one definition (the only other hits are tests/smoke.mjs:805, which just mirrors the shape in a fixture, and a prose comment at tests/e2e.mjs:7). There is no settings control bound to it and no Tauri call consuming it. The shipped windows go the opposite way: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:28, :47, :66 set `"alwaysOnBottom": true` on all three pieces, and tests/e2e.mjs:221-224 asserts the app is deliberately NOT topmost. Note that §12:603 hedges with "optional", so the dead field is the confirmed finding; whether its absence also violates the §22:1060 checkbox is a harder call I am not resolving.

items.contract_clause: §18 technical style / §28 Phase 1 "- read current code," "- document migration risks." CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1205-1210; AGENTS.md:100 "Do not add speculative UI. Ask a focused question or preserve the simpler behavior."
items.implementation: The entire pop-window path is retained but unreachable from the running app. The single entry point is stubbed out: frontend/app.js:16 `async function popOut(){return false}`, with the comment at :13-15 explaining the mechanism was abandoned ("별도 pop 창으로 내보내던 방식은 … 폐지한다"). All seven call sites therefore fall through to the in-window modal: frontend/app.js:423, :451, :674, :738, :800, :979, :981 (`if(await popOut(...))return;`). Consequently the Rust command `open_form` (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:109-150, registered at :391) is never invoked by the frontend — the only invocations in the repo are tests/e2e.mjs:228 and :233. That makes the whole chain dead: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:74-81 `pop_ready`, :84-89 `close_pop` (registered :388-389), :120 the `index.html?w=pop&form=…` URL, :123-148 the pop WebviewWindowBuilder, :278 `.with_denylist(&["pop"])`; frontend/app.js:9 `IS_POP`, :11 `mode-pop` class, :19-25 `closePopSoon` (which invokes `close_pop`), :114 `pop_ready`, :1210-1221 the `form`/`payload` bootstrap; frontend/styles.css:80-86 the six `body.mode-pop` rules. The path is still *reachable by URL* (`index.html?w=pop&form=…`) — tests/smoke.mjs:362-365 navigates it directly — so it is dead with respect to app gestures, not literally unreachable code.

items.contract_clause: "Use official Tauri 2 APIs/plugins and keep capabilities narrowly scoped." — AGENTS.md:60; "- least-privilege fs capability scope," CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1168 (§26)
items.implementation: Both capability files still grant permissions to a window label `"pop"` that no longer exists at runtime: src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:5 `"windows": ["cal", "mini", "status", "pop"]` and src-tauri/capabilities/main.json:5 identical, whose description at :4 explicitly justifies it ("pop 창은 상세(첨부)와 설정(백업)을 담으므로 포함한다"). src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:12-69 declares only `cal`, `mini` and `status`; the `pop` window is only ever created by the dead `open_form` (see DISC-SYS-16). The grant is latent rather than exploitable — a pop window can still be materialised via `open_form` from a privileged context — but it is a stale widening of the capability surface against a least-privilege clause.

items.contract_clause: "6. updated `README.md`," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1260 (§29)
items.implementation: build_windows.ps1:9 is `git diff --exit-code -- web_standalone.html helper_preview.html`, but /home/user/WorkDashboard/helper_preview.html does not exist (ls: No such file or directory) and is never produced — tools/build-standalone.mjs:48 emits exactly one artifact, `['index.html', ['zip.js','combobox.js','core.js','app.js'], 'web_standalone.html']`. The file is a v5 leftover (the v5 inventory at CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:799-800 lists `frontend/helper.html` / `frontend/helper.js`, both now gone). I verified the failure mode: git tolerates the unmatched pathspec, `git diff --exit-code -- web_standalone.html helper_preview.html` returns exit 0, so the drift guard does not break — it simply checks one file fewer than it reads as checking. The equivalent CI step is correct (.github/workflows/windows-build.yml:44 diffs only `web_standalone.html`), so the two guards have silently diverged.

items.contract_clause: "6. updated `README.md`," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1260 (§29)
items.implementation: README.md documents the pop-window architecture that DISC-SYS-16 shows is dead. Exact stale lines: README.md:27 `| 상세 (pop 창) | 지금까지 뭘 했고 다음은 뭔가 | 업무 기록, 첨부, 지출, 절차 전단계 |` — the detail surface is now an in-window modal, not a pop window (frontend/app.js:800 falls through `popOut`); README.md:195 "…조각 창 세 개가 실제로 뜨는지, pop 창이 열리는지," — describes e2e coverage of a path the app no longer takes; README.md:197 "CI의 `windows-e2e` 잡이 돌립니다." — false, that job is workflow_dispatch + opt-in only (see DISC-SYS-07); README.md:204 "?w=cal|mini|status|pop 파라미터로 창마다 필요한 조각만 렌더"; README.md:206 "app.js 화면 UI (조각·팝·드래그·키보드)"; README.md:211 "src-tauri/ Tauri 2 네이티브 셸 (조각 3창·트레이·pop 창), 아이콘, NSIS 설정". The three release-note lines shipped with the installer are consistent with the new behaviour (.github/workflows/windows-build.yml:229-234 "별도 창이 새로 뜨지 않습니다"), which confirms the README is the stale half.

items.contract_clause: §12 "### Deep-link behavior" … "- main should open the corresponding schedule detail automatically." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:611-616
items.implementation: tests/e2e.mjs:236-246 no longer tests what its comment claims. It writes `s.pendingSelection` (:240), waits, then asserts at :246 `check('딥링크가 상세 pop 창을 연다', afterRelay.includes('(pop)'), afterRelay)`. But the consumer at frontend/app.js:1058 calls `openRecord(sel.kind, sel.id)`, which at frontend/app.js:800 hits the stubbed `popOut` and opens an in-window modal — no `(pop)` window is created by the deep link. The assertion can still pass, because the pop window opened 16 lines earlier by the direct `open_form` call (tests/e2e.mjs:228-232, form 'schedule') is still on screen and `closePopSoon` only fires once its modal stack empties (frontend/app.js:19-25, :124). So the check is vacuous — it observes the earlier window. Marked probable: I did not run the suite (it is Windows-only and CI-disabled, DISC-SYS-07/08), so the precise pass/fail is inferred from the control flow rather than observed. The neighbouring assertion at :244 (`소비 후 딥링크 상태가 비워진다`) is genuine.

items.contract_clause: "The current Rust code already uses `--helper-only`; audit and preserve/fix this behavior." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1159 (§25); "### OS autostart" / "- launch with helper-only argument," / "- main stays hidden," :1152-1155; §22 H "- [ ] Autostart helper-only mode works." :1061
items.implementation: `--helper-only` no longer exists. A grep for `helper-only|helper_only` across src-tauri/ returns zero hits; src-tauri/src/lib.rs:12 defines `const PIECES: [&str; 3] = ["cal", "mini", "status"];` and the autostart plugin is initialised with no launch arguments at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:272 `.plugin(tauri_plugin_autostart::init(MacosLauncher::LaunchAgent, None))`. Autostart itself works (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:160-175 `set_autostart`/`is_autostart_enabled`, exercised at tests/e2e.mjs:200-212), but it starts the full three-piece app, not a helper-only mode. The contract says "preserve/fix", and the behaviour was removed rather than preserved; whether the three-piece redesign moots the clause is not something the contract addresses, so I am reporting the removal, not adjudicating it.

items.contract_clause: "1. Main screen = **left upcoming D-day vendor cards + right monthly calendar**." — AGENTS.md:21; "14. The desktop helper window must remain minimal…" AGENTS.md:39; "- Main and helper windows must share state reliably." AGENTS.md:57; "Current Tauri configuration already defines a small `helper` window. Preserve the concept and improve behavior." CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:581; "Tauri main window currently starts around 1380×900. This is acceptable as a baseline…" :196
items.implementation: The main-window + helper-window architecture the contract presupposes has been replaced by three decoration-less always-on-bottom desktop pieces. src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:12-69 declares labels `cal` (964x700), `mini` (362x700) and `status` (362x284), every one with `"decorations": false`, `"alwaysOnBottom": true`, `"skipTaskbar": true`; there is no window labelled `main` or `helper` anywhere. frontend/app.js:3-6 states the intent outright: "이 앱에는 메인 창이 없다" ("this app has no main window"). The release notes shipped to users say the same (.github/workflows/windows-build.yml:181 "[이 앱에는 창이 없습니다]"). I am flagging the architectural fact against the clauses that name a main window and a helper window; the contract never authorises or forbids this specific restructuring, so whether it is a violation or an unreviewed redesign is genuinely open — hence probable rather than confirmed.

items.contract_clause: §28 Phase 1 "- read current code," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1207; §30 "choose **clarity and fewer interactions**." :1279
items.implementation: frontend/app.js:2 initialises `let currentMonth=new Date(2026,7,1);` — a hardcoded August 2026 — which is dead: frontend/app.js:1184 unconditionally overwrites it during bootstrap with `const d=C.parse(C.todayISO()); currentMonth=new Date(d.getFullYear(),d.getMonth(),1); render();` before any render that reads it. The literal is a leftover of the contract-freeze era (2026-08-14) and has no runtime effect, but it is a live trap: any future code path that renders before line 1184 would display August 2026.

items.contract_clause: "1. Main screen = **left upcoming D-day vendor cards + right monthly calendar**." — AGENTS.md:21; reinforced by CODEX_START_PROMPT.txt:9 "The required main UI is left-side upcoming vendor D-day cards plus a large vertically-scrollable monthly calendar." and the ASCII layout at CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:122-140 (left column "다가오는 일정", right column calendar).
items.implementation: There is no main screen at all, and the two halves are mirrored. src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:12-69 declares three windowless always-on-bottom widgets (`cal` x=96, `mini` x=1080, `status` x=1080/y=776) and no main window. frontend/app.js:4 states outright: "이 앱에는 메인 창이 없다" ("this app has no main window"). In the single-page/browser composition frontend/styles.css:58-60 lays out `.desk{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 352px}` with `.piece-cal{grid-row:1/3}` as the first child — i.e. calendar LEFT, vendor cards RIGHT. src-tauri/src/lib.rs:225-227 does the same in Tauri: `place("cal", mp.x + gutter, ...)` then `place("mini", right_x, ...)`, `place("status", right_x, ...)`. The contracted left rail is on the right, and the contracted right calendar is on the left, in a separate OS window.

items.contract_clause: "6. The calendar body must be vertically scrollable; do not compress week rows until text becomes unreadable." — AGENTS.md:26. Also CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:262-264 "Calendar body itself is vertically scrollable. / Week row/day-cell height is allowed to grow to preserve readable event text. / Do not shrink event text to unreadable sizes just to force the entire month into one viewport." and :633 "month week rows are not artificially squashed."
items.implementation: The calendar body is explicitly non-scrollable and sized to the window. frontend/styles.css:124 `.calendar-scroll{flex:1;min-height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0 10px 10px}` — `overflow:hidden`, despite the element id `calendarScroll` (frontend/index.html:18). frontend/styles.css:125 `.month-grid{...grid-auto-rows:minmax(0,1fr);gap:3px;height:100%}` forces all week rows to divide the fixed window height. The code comment at frontend/styles.css:121-123 states the intent verbatim: "minmax(0,1fr) 이면 6주 달은 94px, 5주 달은 113px 로 저절로 맞고 스크롤이 없다" ("...fits automatically and there is no scroll"). frontend/styles.css:126 `.day{...overflow:hidden}` clips whatever does not fit in the squashed row.

items.contract_clause: "- Weekday header remains visible/sticky while the calendar body scrolls." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:261; "- right calendar has one vertical scroll container, / - weekday header is sticky inside that container," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:630-632.
items.implementation: The weekday header is not inside the scroll container and is not sticky. frontend/index.html:17-18 places `<div class="weekdays">` as a sibling BEFORE `<div class="calendar-scroll" id="calendarScroll">`, and frontend/styles.css:117 styles it `.weekdays{flex:0 0 auto;display:grid;...}` with no `position:sticky` anywhere in the file. (Moot in practice only because DISC-UI-02 removed scrolling entirely.)

items.contract_clause: "2. Do not add KPI cards, progress percentages, analytics, charts, status dashboards, ..." — AGENTS.md:22; "Do **not** add: / - KPI cards, / - progress percentages, / - progress bars," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:82-86; "No progress bar. No project-health status. No invented state badge." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:250; "Do not add KPI cards, progress percentages, analytics, arbitrary status filters, vendor color coding, or dashboard widgets that are not explicitly required." — CODEX_START_PROMPT.txt:7.
items.implementation: Percentages and meter bars are computed and rendered in three places. frontend/app.js:209 `const pct=g.stepsTotal?Math.round(g.stepsDone/g.stepsTotal*100):0;` then :212 ``. frontend/app.js:244 same `pct` computation, rendered at :250 as `` — an explicit "진행 N%" progress bar on every vendor row. frontend/app.js:309/315 repeats it for the 행사 board. frontend/app.js:207 renders a roll-up KPI line `${gs.length}건 · 진행 ${done}/${total}`; :217 renders a budget KPI `잔액 …원`. Supporting CSS: frontend/styles.css:280-283 `.st-meter .track i`, :302-303 `.bh-bar i{...}`, :491-495 `.bg-bar i`.

items.contract_clause: "4. D-day belongs in the **left vendor cards and detail surfaces**, not inside the calendar event label." — AGENTS.md:24; "Do **not** include D-day in the event label." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:291; §2.4 "**Wrong** / `대한건설 · D-2`" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:110-111.
items.implementation: The calendar event label carries a D-day badge. frontend/app.js:526 `const dd=r.planned?'':C.ddayClass(r),badge=MODE_C==='full'?(r.planned?'예상':(dd==='overdue'||dd==='today'?C.ddayLabel(r):'')):'';` and :527 emits it inside the event button: `...${label}${badge?`${C.esc(badge)}`:''}`. `C.ddayLabel` produces the `D-?`/`D+?` string. Styled at frontend/styles.css:165 `.ev-d{flex:0 0 auto;font-size:var(--fs-xs);font-weight:700}`. Scope is limited to overdue/today events in wide cells, but the contract's prohibition is unconditional.

items.contract_clause: "3. The calendar event text must show **`vendor name · actual schedule/task name`**, not `D-?`." — AGENTS.md:23; "Display: / `업체명 · 일정명`" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:281-283; "Prefer showing real event names over collapsing too early." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:646; "Do not shrink event text to unreadable sizes just to force the entire month into one viewport." — :264.
items.implementation: The vendor name is conditionally dropped, and at narrow widths all text is dropped. frontend/app.js:502 `const chipMode=w=>w>=170?'full':(w>=110?'name':'dot');` frontend/app.js:524 `const label=MODE_C==='full'?`${C.esc(v?.name||L.noVendor)} · ${C.esc(r.name)}`:C.esc(r.name);` — below a 170px cell the label degrades to the task name only (no vendor). frontend/app.js:519-520: below a 110px cell the whole `.events` list is replaced by `<button class="dot ..."></button>` markers plus a count `<b class="dot-n">`, i.e. zero event text in the calendar. The author's comment at :493-496 acknowledges the tradeoff ("좁으면 글자를 포기하고 점과 건수로 물러난다" — "when narrow, give up the text and fall back to dots and a count"). Cell width is derived from the window (`cellWidth()` at :497-501), which is itself fixed because of DISC-UI-02, so a narrowed `cal` window silently erases the contracted label.

items.contract_clause: "7. Clicking an **empty date cell** must open “Add schedule” with that date already selected." — AGENTS.md:21-40 item 7, AGENTS.md:27; "Clicking unused space in an in-month date cell must open the Add Schedule modal with: / - date prefilled," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:301-303; "- blank day area -> add schedule" — :938; "Click a blank calendar date -> create schedule -> event appears on that exact date." — AGENTS.md:88.
items.implementation: A single click does nothing; the shipped handler requires a DOUBLE click. frontend/app.js:534 `cell.addEventListener('dblclick',e=>{if(e.target.closest('[data-event-id]'))return;openSchedule(ds)});` — there is no `click` listener on the day cell (the only `click` listeners in renderCalendar are on `[data-more-day]`, `[data-done-day]`, `[data-event-id]` at :542-545). The deviation is deliberate per the comment at :532-533 ("DesktopCal 관례대로 빈 날짜는 두 번 클릭으로 연다"). The affordance shown on hover, frontend/app.js:530 `+ ${state.terms.event}` / frontend/styles.css:192-193, does not disclose that a double click is required. Date IS correctly prefilled once opened (`openSchedule(ds)`), so only the click gesture deviates.

items.contract_clause: "Do not add a `+N` collapse merely because there are four events." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:650; "Because the calendar itself can scroll, allow day/week height to grow with content." — :648.
items.implementation: frontend/app.js:504 `const MODE_C=chipMode(cellWidth()),CAP=MODE_C==='full'?3:2;` and :522-528 `const show=open.slice(0,CAP),rest=open.length-show.length; ... (rest>0?`<button class="more" data-more-day="${ds}">＋${rest}건</button>`:'')`. With four events in a wide cell exactly the prohibited `＋1건` collapse appears; in a medium-width cell it collapses at three. Row height cannot grow with content because of DISC-UI-02. The contract's one mitigation IS satisfied — "Any overflow UI must still allow a one-click view of all events on that date" (:650) — via frontend/app.js:542 `openDay(b.dataset.moreDay)`.

items.contract_clause: "# 27. Out of scope for this iteration / Do not add these unless separately requested: ... - construction-cost management, / - budget/payment accounting," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:1177-1187.
items.implementation: A full budget/expenditure accounting subsystem ships as one of the three desktop pieces. frontend/index.html:53-57 declares the 예산 section inside the `status` window (including a `합본예산서` creation button); frontend/index.html:96-113 declares `#budgetModal` (budget title/year/line items) and `#spendModal` (amount, spent-vs-planned status, date, vendor, linked project). Logic: frontend/app.js:216-226 (budget summary, `잔액`/`초과` figures, `budgetBarInner` spend/plan meter), :273-299 (`won`, `budgetBar`, `budgetFigures`, `spendRows`, `budgetGroups`), :354 total accumulation, :452-490 (`openSpend`, save, `deleteSpend`). It is also injected into the required detail modal at frontend/app.js:808 `${spendSection(selectedRecord)}` with an `detailAddSpend` button (:355, :812). Money is surfaced on the vendor board too: frontend/app.js:250 `${L.vendorSpendLine(...)}`. Data model carries it: frontend/core.js:72 terms include `budgetItem:'예산항목',spend:'지출'`.

items.contract_clause: "Do not infer missing product requirements from generic dashboard conventions." — AGENTS.md:7; "Do not add speculative UI. Ask a focused question or preserve the simpler behavior." — AGENTS.md:100; "... or other invented management states." — AGENTS.md:22; "- invented work-state taxonomies." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:93.
items.implementation: A 행사/group ("event") dimension exists that appears nowhere in the contract — grepping 행사|group|Group across AGENTS.md and CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md returns only unrelated hits ("## 4.3 Visual noise budget", "- budget/payment accounting,", "- must have a clear drag area"). Shipped: frontend/index.html:48-52 the 행사 section of the status piece; frontend/app.js:205-215 `renderStatus` group summaries; :303-340 `renderGroupBoard` with its own expand/collapse board, per-group vendor counts, done counts, overdue counts and progress bar; :517 `day-bands` painting group period bands across calendar cells (frontend/styles.css:185-191); frontend/core.js:99 label `viewGroup:'행사별'`. The contract is silent on this concept, so it is added UI, not contracted UI. Confidence is "probable" rather than "confirmed" only because contractual silence is not an explicit prohibition — AGENTS.md:100 is the closest binding text.

items.contract_clause: "## 5.2 Header / Recommended height: 56–64 px. / Left: / - app title: `업체별 업무 일정` / - optional one-line microcopy, visually subordinate / Right: / - `D-day 도우미` / - `템플릿` / - `설정` / - `+ 업무` / - primary `+ 일정`" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:198-211; "- Primary controls remain in stable positions." — :164; "header is fixed within app layout," — :629.
items.implementation: There is no application header and the listed controls are scattered across two separate OS windows. Grepping `업체별 업무 일정` across frontend/ finds it only in the document `<title>` (frontend/index.html:1) and as a data string in frontend/core.js:72 and :214 — it is never rendered as an on-screen app title. `+ 일정` lives in the cal window header (frontend/index.html:15 `#addScheduleBtn`), while `+ 업무`, `템플릿` and `설정` live in the mini window's footer (frontend/index.html:37-41 `.mini-tools`). `D-day 도우미` does not exist (see DISC-UI-14). Because §5.2's height is hedged ("Recommended") but the control inventory is not, this is recorded as missing rather than a hedge deviation.

items.contract_clause: "Header: / - title `다가오는 일정` / - D-day horizon selector" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:219-222; "Overdue dates naturally appear before today; do not create a separate status category/tab." — :237.
items.implementation: The D-day rail header has no `다가오는 일정` title (grep finds the string nowhere in frontend/). frontend/index.html:25 puts a two-way view tablist in its place: `<div class="tabs seg" role="tablist" aria-label="미니 대시보드 보기"><button ... data-board="due"><button ... data-board="vendor">`, labelled 일정순 / 업체별 (frontend/core.js:99). The horizon selector IS present and complete (frontend/index.html:27, including 무제한/직접설정). Whether the 일정순/업체별 toggle counts as the prohibited "separate status category/tab" is ambiguous — :237 names status categories specifically, and this tab switches grouping, not status — so confidence is probable for the tab half; the missing title is confirmed.

items.contract_clause: "Card contents — keep it strict: / ```text / 대한건설                         D-2 / 안전보건수준평가 / 8.14. · 배수로 정비공사 / ```" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:242-248; priority order "1. vendor/company name, / 2. actual schedule/task name," — :155-156.
items.implementation: The shipped card collapses the contracted vendor line and task line into a single line. frontend/app.js:150-152: `${C.esc(v?.name||L.noVendor)} · ${C.esc(r.name)}` followed by `${spanText(r)}${p?` · ${C.esc(p.name)}`:''}` and `${C.ddayLabel(r)}`. Both lines are single-line-ellipsised (frontend/styles.css:236-237 `white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis`), so in a 352px-wide rail the vendor name and the task name compete for one line and the task name is what gets truncated — inverting the visual hierarchy of :155-156. The card also carries an extra inline `✓` complete button not in the contracted shape (frontend/app.js:158).

items.contract_clause: "14. The desktop helper window must remain minimal: vendor, nearest task, date, D-day. No dashboard clutter." — AGENTS.md:39; "Current helper click merely opens/focuses the main window. Improve this: / - clicking a helper card should open/focus main, / - main should open the corresponding schedule detail automatically." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:613-616; "Click helper card -> main window opens focused on the corresponding detail." — AGENTS.md:96; "Open helper -> it uses the same D-day horizon/state as main app." — AGENTS.md:95.
items.implementation: No helper window and no main window exist, so the contracted helper→main deep link is unimplementable as specified. src-tauri/src/lib.rs:12 `const PIECES: [&str; 3] = ["cal", "mini", "status"];` — no `helper` label; src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:14/34/52 confirms the three labels. The tray menu offers only `toggle-cal` / `toggle-mini` / `toggle-status` (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:362-364). The nearest analogue, the `mini` piece, is not minimal in the contracted sense: it also carries a view tablist, an overdue pill, an omni search combobox and three footer tool buttons (frontend/index.html:25-41). Clicking a mini card opens the detail modal inside the mini window itself (frontend/app.js:159 → `openRecord`), since cross-window pop-out was disabled at frontend/app.js:16.

items.contract_clause: "- Avoid nested cards and excessive badges/chips." — AGENTS.md:47; "On the default main view, avoid: / - multiple badge systems, ... / - secondary filters that are not essential." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:171-179; "... or other invented management states." — AGENTS.md:22.
items.implementation: Several coexisting badge systems render on the default view. frontend/app.js:146-147 an overdue count pill `지남 ${late}` / `지남 없음` (frontend/styles.css:246-248) — a derived management count the contract does not define. frontend/app.js:232 and :324 a per-row step-count badge `${it.stepsDone}/${it.stepsTotal}` (frontend/styles.css:321). frontend/app.js:250 an overdue sub-badge `` plus a money badge `` on the same row as the progress bar. frontend/app.js:515 a `done-mark` `✓N` chip in the day cell head. frontend/app.js:526-527 the `ev-d` D-day chip (DISC-UI-05). frontend/index.html:29-34 adds an omni search/filter combobox to the rail. Nested cards: frontend/styles.css:288 `.board-row{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:#fff}` sits inside `.piece` (:61-63), and `.bg-project`/`.bg-vendor` nest a third level inside the budget board. Marked probable because "excessive" and "essential" are the contract's own undefined thresholds.

items.contract_clause: "- Work-tool aesthetic, not a decorative consumer dashboard." — AGENTS.md:44; "- Default palette is neutral/light." — AGENTS.md:45; "## 19.1 Tone / - Korean government/office utility, / - calm, / - precise, / - neutral, / - not flashy," — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:884-890; "- neutral warm/cool background, / - white panels," — :897-898.
items.implementation: The page background is a decorative three-layer wallpaper, not a neutral ground: frontend/styles.css:51-57 `body{background: radial-gradient(1200px 500px at 75% -10%, #ffe9c7 0%, transparent 55%), radial-gradient(1600px 900px at 20% 110%, #1e5b48 0%, transparent 60%), linear-gradient(180deg,#8db8d8 0%, #bcd3e2 38%, #dde5d2 62%, #6f9c7c 100%); background-attachment:fixed;}`, and panels are translucent "glass" rather than white: :28-31 `--glass:rgba(249,250,252,.97); --cell:rgba(255,255,255,.92)` with `--shadow:0 10px 34px rgba(19,20,22,.20)` (:22). This is confined to the browser/preview composition — frontend/styles.css:73 `body.win-mode{background:transparent}` removes it in Tauri, where the real Windows desktop shows through instead. The accent-color rules ARE honored: a single `--accent:#0b50d0` (:14), red reserved for `--danger` urgency (:18), and grepping for per-vendor color assignment (hsl(/hue/vendorColor/palette) across frontend/ returns nothing — AGENTS.md:46 "Do not assign arbitrary colors per vendor" is satisfied. Marked probable because "decorative" and "not flashy" are qualitative and the wallpaper never ships in the Tauri target.

items.contract_clause: "8. Clicking a D-day card or calendar event must open a **detail dialog/popover**, not navigate to a new page." — AGENTS.md:28 — this clause is SATISFIED, but the disabled cross-window pop-out left its Rust half in place. Relevant obligation: "Use official Tauri 2 APIs/plugins and keep capabilities narrowly scoped." — AGENTS.md:61.
items.implementation: frontend/app.js:16 `async function popOut(){return false}` unconditionally disables the pop-out path, so all seven call sites (frontend/app.js:423, 451, 674, 738, 800, 979, 981) fall through to the in-place modal — AGENTS.md:28 holds. But the Rust side is now unreachable: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:109 `fn open_form(app, form, payload)` builds an `index.html?w=pop&form=...` window (:120, :135) and is registered in the invoke handler at :391, yet grepping `open_form` across frontend/ returns zero hits. `pop_ready` (:75) and `close_pop` (:85) survive only because frontend/app.js:24 still calls `close_pop` from `closePopSoon`, which itself returns immediately when `IS_POP` is false (:20) — and no code path can now set `IS_POP`. The `pop` window mode CSS (frontend/styles.css:80-86) is likewise unreachable.

items.contract_clause: "At startup / Today button: / - move current month into view, / - position Today reasonably near the visible center of the calendar scroll area." — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:637-640; "- Today -> current month + scroll Today into good visible position" — :939.
items.implementation: The month-switch half is implemented, the scroll-positioning half cannot be and is absent. frontend/app.js:1061 `$('todayBtn').addEventListener('click',()=>{const d=C.parse(C.todayISO());currentMonth=new Date(d.getFullYear(),d.getMonth(),1);renderCalendar()})` and frontend/app.js:1184 at startup set the month but never scroll — there is no `scrollTo`/`scrollIntoView` call against `#calendarScroll` anywhere in frontend/app.js. This follows directly from DISC-UI-02 (`overflow:hidden`, so there is no scroll offset to set). Whether this is separately a violation is arguable — with the whole month always visible, Today is trivially "in view" — hence it is reported as a missing sub-behavior of the scroll clause rather than an independent defect.

items.contract_clause: "Keep a migration path from existing v5 state." — AGENTS.md:56; "# 15. Data model target (v6 suggested)" — CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIEF.md:654 (note: §15 is explicitly hedged as "suggested").
items.implementation: The shipped document title still advertises v5 while the app is at 0.7.0. frontend/index.html:1 `<title>업체별 업무 일정 v5</title>`, versus src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:5 `"version": "0.7.0"`. The title is what the Windows taskbar/window manager shows for the browser-mode page. Purely a stale label — no behavioral consequence found.

protected_paths_note: hook 으로 강제하지 않는다 (CLAUDE.md §6). visual/baseline/ 과 tests/acceptance/ 는 아직 존재하지 않는다.
not_created_in_this_task: visual/baseline/  — 사용자가 생성을 지시하지 않았다. 보호 목록에만 등재.
IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md — 계약 §29-8 이 요구하지만 제품 산출물이므로 이번 범위 밖 (DISC-SYS-10).
